title: Recognize and Use Similar Triangles
description: Identify similar triangles from matching angles, pair corresponding sides, set up proportions, and solve the right-triangle altitude configuration without mentally rotating the triangles.

questions.stem_html: Triangles ABC and DEF are similar, with A matching D, B matching E, and C matching F. AB = 7, DE = 21, and BC = 10. What is EF?
questions.explanation_html: AB corresponds to DE and BC corresponds to EF. The multiplier from ABC to DEF is 3, so EF = 10 × 3.
questions.variation: Match corresponding sides in two named similar triangles

questions.stem_html: In triangle ABC, D lies on AB and E lies on AC. Segment DE is parallel to BC. AD = 6, DB = 12, and DE = 8. What is BC?
questions.explanation_html: Parallel lines give matching angles for ADE and ABC. The multiplier from AD to AB is (6 + 12)/6 = 3. Apply it from DE to BC.
questions.variation: Use parallel lines to identify the inner triangle and its scale

questions.stem_html: Right triangle ABC is right at C. The altitude from C meets hypotenuse AB at D. If AD = 9 and DB = 25, what is CD?
questions.explanation_html: The two smaller triangles are similar. Their corresponding sides give CD² = AD × DB = 225, hence CD = 15.
questions.variation: Use the similar triangles to find the right-triangle altitude

questions.stem_html: Right triangle ABC is right at C. Altitude CD meets AB at D. If CD = 35 and AD = 25, what is DB?
questions.explanation_html: Match corresponding sides of the two smaller triangles. CD² = AD × DB, so dividing 1225 by 25 gives 49.
questions.variation: Recover a missing hypotenuse segment from the altitude

questions.stem_html: Right triangle ABC is right at C. Altitude CD meets AB at D. If AD = 25 and DB = 144, what is AC?
questions.explanation_html: AB = 169. Similar triangles ACD and ABC give AC² = AD × AB = 4225. The positive length is 65.
questions.variation: Find a leg by pairing the large and small right triangles
